Nature & food

melon noun

also sweet melon

classical

Plīn. NH XIX 65
Vulg. Num. 11, 5

pepō, peponis m.

noun, third declension

sweet melon

The Greek oblique stem (πέπων, -ονος) keeps its o short.

Other words

  • 1mēlopepō, mēlopeponis: short o in the oblique stem (Lewis & Short mēlopepo, -ōnis). The shared Greek stem πέπων, -ονος; Lewis & Short itself prints pepo, -ŏnis.

    mēlopepō1, mēlopeponis m. — the apple-shaped melon

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plīn. NH XIX 67

  • mēlō, mēlōnis m.

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Pallad. IV 9, 6

    The late shortening of mēlopepō, the ancestor of the modern melon-words.

See also watermelon, pumpkin.

SourcesLewis & Short: pepo · Lewis & Short: melopepo · Lewis & Short: melo
